data.name: Avtar
data.long_meaning: Avtar means 'descent' or 'incarnation'. In Hindu mythology, it refers to the manifestation of a deity on earth in human or animal form to save humanity.

in_sanskrit.name: अवतार
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: The act of coming down from heaven to earth, the descent of a deity or a divine being on earth in human form, the embodiment of a god or goddess in the physical world, the manifestation of God in a human being, the incarnation of a deity, a divine descent or a descent from a high place to a lower one.

in_hindi.name: अवतार
in_hindi.long_meaning: एक देव या दिव्य व्यक्ति को पृथ्वी पर आने वा स्वरूप को पृथ्वी पर लौटना, एक देव या दिव्य व्यक्ति के पुरुषवतार या शरीरी रूप में पृथ्वी पर अवतरण का कारण होना, देवता या दिव्यता का प्रकाश, देवता या दिव्यता की पुरानी विरासत वा अपने स्वतंत्र रूप से पृथ्वी पर निवास करना, एक देव या दिव्य व्यक्ति का स्वरूप को पृथ्वी पर लौटना, देवता या दिव्यता का अवतार, अवतरण या उत्पत्ति, एक उच्चता स्थान से अधः जाने वा उत्पत्ति, अवतारण या उत्पत्ति का कारण होना.

data.cultural_impact: The term Avtar holds immense cultural significance in Hinduism. It is a symbol of divine intervention and belief in the power of the gods to protect and save their people. The concept of Avtar is also an integral part of Hindu traditions and mythology, with numerous stories and beliefs surrounding it.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Avtar represents the idea of the divine presence in the material world. It is a reminder that even in times of darkness and hardship, the divine is always present and ready to intervene and offer guidance and protection. The belief in the Avtar also reinforces the idea of faith and devotion, encouraging individuals to turn towards the divine for strength and guidance.

historical_references.reference: The concept of Avatars originated in Hindu mythology, specifically in Puranic literature. It refers to the descent of a deity on earth in human or animal form to correct a disturbance in the world order (Dharma). This belief is grounded in the idea that the deity descends to restore balance and save humanity from imminent doom. The most popular Avatars are the ten incarnations of Vishnu, known as the Dashavatars.

Another well-known Avatar is Rama, the hero of the epic Ramayana. He is considered an Avatar of Vishnu, who descended to earth to fight the demon king Ravana and protect his wife Sita. This epic is believed to have been composed between the 5th and 2nd century BCE, and it highlights the importance of Dharma (duty, moral virtue) in Hindu society.

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's interconnected world, the name Avtar continues to be cherished by Hindu families globally. It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Hindu name websites where expectant parents research meaningful names. The name bridges traditional Hindu values with modern Indian identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and cultural significance.
